subject: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04 09:12 PDT
Subject: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification

Hi team,

Quick note — Brightline returned redlines on the draft Order Form and flagged a concern about the security exhibit language: they want an explicit carveout for their regulated lab environment and are pushing back on broad "inspection rights" language. Key asks from them: a narrower SOC 2 evidence set, a maximum 48-hour pen-test notice window, and limited staging access for external testers.

I've attached their redlines (RFQ_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a first-pass pen-test scope they shared (pen-test-scope-draft.xlsx). Can legal confirm whether we can: 
- Offer a scoped inspection band (samples) instead of full system inspection,
- Limit pen-test notice to 48 hrs only if the test is non-intrusive / read-only, otherwise retain the standard 7-day notice for production-affecting tests, and
- Use timeboxed staging access for evidence collection plus an ops-runbook for any requested artifacts?

Karthik — can you advise if these carveouts are acceptable from a risk/assurance perspective? Laura & Soojin — any redlines we should push in the MSA / security exhibit to preserve our audit posture?

Goal: short internal sync and then a single-thread reply to Brightline with a clear position and fallback.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RFQ_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf, pen-test-scope-draft.xlsx
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightlinetx.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Price <aaron.price@brightlinetx.com>
Date: 2027-05-04 10:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification

Connor,

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for attaching the redlines. A couple of clarifications from our side before legal digs in: 

- Our labs are subject to client contracts that prohibit third-party full-system inspections — that’s why we’re requesting sampling only.
- Our internal security team can accept a 7-day notice for high-impact pen tests but has asked for a 48-hour window for low-impact code audits or scans.
- For evidence, we prefer a defined artifact list (SOC 2 relevant artifacts + specific log exports) rather than open-ended evidence requests.

If you can accept a bounded exhibit that lists allowed artifacts, a pen-test categorization (low/medium/high) with corresponding notice windows, and a staging access runbook for limited handoffs, that will keep procurement moving.

Appreciate you coordinating.

— Maria
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Brightline Therapeutics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04 11:25 PDT
Subject: Re: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification

Connor / team,

I reviewed the attachments. High-level thoughts:
1) Sampling vs full inspection — OK to offer sampled evidence provided we: document sampling methodology, include a minimum set of SOC 2 artifacts (control owner, evidence location, log extracts), and reserve the right to request additional evidence via formal legal channels if we have cause.

2) Pen-test notice windows — propose a three-tier approach: low (48 hrs), medium (7 days), high (14 days + pre-test coordination with ops). Define criteria for each tier (non-intrusive scans vs credentialed tests vs simulated phishing / exploit attempts). This protects us operationally.

3) Staging access & runbook — approve timeboxed, monitored staging with scoped credentials; require test plans and a named POC from the customer. No open shell access in production.

4) MSA language — we should push to keep language that preserves our ability to deny access if a test would materially affect service or violate other customers’ privacy. Suggest redline language and fallback: allow scoped evidence and staged tests, deny unlimited inspection.

I can draft the updated exhibit and tier definitions for you all to review.

Karthik
Head of Applied ML Ops Risk
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05 09:08 PDT
Subject: Re: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification

Thanks — I like Karthik's structure. A few legal points to include in the draft:

- Add an evidence request scoring clause: requests tied to SOC 2 sections (CC1–CC7) will be triaged; anything outside that scope requires a legal sign-off.
- Keep explicit exclusion for "forensic access" unless subpoenaed/ordered.
- For pen tests, we should add an acceptance matrix: customer provides plan, we confirm categorization within 24 hrs, notice windows apply from confirmation. Also include a provision for emergency testing (e.g., active compromise) where we can require immediate coordination.
- Limit the number of live test days per rolling 12 months (e.g., 5 days) unless under an escalated SLA.

I'll incorporate redline text and propose specific wording for the notice windows and the sampling methodology. Connor — worth a short sync with Brightline to agree the tiers before we send the redline back.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-06 14:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Order Form assurance scope — pen-test carveouts & evidence sprint clarification

Maria / Aaron — thanks for the context and fast replies. Looping in our legal and risk leads so we can align on a concise proposal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 20-min call tomorrow to align on the three-tier pen-test categorization (Connor + Maria + Aaron + Karthik + Laura) — does 10:30am PT on 2027-05-07 work?
2) Redwood will circulate an updated security exhibit draft post-call that:
   - Enumerates permitted artifacts for SOC 2 evidence (logs, control mappings, key config exports),
   - Defines low/medium/high pen-test tiers with notice windows (48 hrs / 7 days / 14 days) and criteria,
   - Includes a timeboxed staging access process and a cap on live test days (5 days / 12 months).
3) If Brightline agrees to the exhibit language, we will mark the Order Form redlines as accepted and proceed to signature.

Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above; DocuSign link to follow after exhibit agreed.
